Messages.Author: Roberto Ullfig
Messages.Body:
Got my handy rules in the mail last night. They could be a little better
written, had to go through them twice. A couple of questions...

1. Say a minion attempts to intercept and the active minion has a +1 stealth.
Now the intercepting minion plays a card that gives +2 to the intercept.
Can the active minion play *2* +1 cards to negate that? The rules seem to
imply that cards are played in "alternating" fashion and that only *1* card
can be played in response to another card.

2. When a minion plays a political card, just *when* can another minion attempt
to block? The rules say before the "terms" of the vote. Does this mean before
the political card is actually revealed or before the voting is done?

3. Can you play poltical cards during a blood hunt vote to increase your votes?

4. Do you refill your hand immediately after *every* card is played (except
during voting)? So, during combat you can play a maneuver, then draw, etc...

5. The rules say that the games take ~3 hours (whatever that means) but it
would seem to me that the games go quicker since your hand is constantly
being refilled. What makes the games take longer than Magic?

--

>would seem to me that the games go quicker since your hand is constantly
>being refilled. What makes the games take longer than Magic?

Haven't played yet, but I would guess that the "blood pool" makes
games last longer since it takes time to "power up" vampires to get
them into play and it's also hard to replenish your blood pool, which
can limit the number of actions you can perform, and so in some sense
you have to play more "conservatively". Also, I would imagine that the
"3 hours" mentioned in the rulebook probably refers to a multi-player
game, rather than a 1-on-1 duel.

Messages.Author: Tom Fontaine
Messages.Body:
In article <32qclo$oa4@fnnews.fnal.gov> ullfig@fnrobo.fnal.gov (Roberto Ullfig) writes:
>Got my handy rules in the mail last night. They could be a little better
>written, had to go through them twice. A couple of questions...

This is not an Official Response (tm) -- I'm not sure if there is a
Jyhad netrep yet -- I don't imagine Tom Wylie could possibly find the
time to do it.  The answers below reflect the way Jyhad was played
when our group playtested the game.

>1. Say a minion attempts to intercept and the active minion has a +1 stealth.
>Now the intercepting minion plays a card that gives +2 to the intercept.
>Can the active minion play *2* +1 cards to negate that? The rules seem to
>imply that cards are played in "alternating" fashion and that only *1* card
>can be played in response to another card.

Good point.  I believe the intent is to alternate 'one-ups' as opposed
to alternating cards.


>2. When a minion plays a political card, just *when* can another minion attempt
>to block? The rules say before the "terms" of the vote. Does this mean before
>the political card is actually revealed or before the voting is done?

After a card is revealed and before the voting is done.


>3. Can you play poltical cards during a blood hunt vote to increase your votes?

Yes.  Or cash the Edge.


>4. Do you refill your hand immediately after *every* card is played (except
>during voting)? So, during combat you can play a maneuver, then draw, etc...

Unless a card explicitly says not to refill, you refill your hand
immediately.  


>5. The rules say that the games take ~3 hours (whatever that means) but it
>would seem to me that the games go quicker since your hand is constantly
>being refilled. What makes the games take longer than Magic?

One of the trickier aspects of the game is that you're sacrificing
your *own* blood to take certain actions.  You simply have a limited
supply of blood, and the nastier cards will typically require blood to
use.  Therefore, cycling is not necessarily an advantage -- every card
you use which requires blood payment brings you closer to death.

Some other reasons: Jyhad is primarily a multiplayer game.  It's more
'epic' than Magic, requiring (IMHO) more subtelty, patience, and
finesse.  Landslide victories are a LOT less common than in Magic (eg,
there's no equivalent of 'mana constipation').  You may find that
seemingly slow and innocuous maneuvers by your opponents are leading
up to something much bigger...

Have fun,
Tom Fontaine

Messages.Author: Matt Rollefson
Messages.Body:
In rec.games.deckmaster ai231@FreeNet.Carleton.CA (Robert Collins) writes:

>I have some question of my own. I just started so I'm having problems even
>phrasing the questions so they make sense.

>6. The area I find most confusing is combat. If two minions get into a
>fight and have plenty of blood to survive does the fight end after one
>round automatically ( doing little damage ) unless one or the other plays a
>press or strike?

Sort of. There are two issues. The first is how strikes work, the
second is whether additional combat rounds are going to ensue.

You normally have one strike. In the choose strike phase, you can
choose to use a card, equipment, or your natural hand strike. You can
only choose one of these methods. There may be additional limitations,
depending on the cards you use. See 15.1, Choose strike.

You can play cards which will grant you additional strikes. This
allows additional damage during a single *round* of combat.

If you want to continue the combat after all strikes in a round have
been resolved, you must press. From the rulebook, 15.1, Press: "If you
want another round of combat, then you must play a press."

>7. If so since both survived does that mean the action ( i.e. hunting )
>succeded or not.

Even though both survived, the action fails. From the rulebook, 15:
"If a player's minion's action *is* blocked, the action is considered
unsuccessful and no cost is paid attempting it, though any action card
used is burned."

Note that hunting by default has a +1 to Stealth, so you would have to
use an intercept effect to block it.

>8. If the active minion does not play a combat card and then the blocking
>player does can the active player play one before damage dealing?

This is my big issue currently with the rules: in what order are
strikes declared? It can make a big difference in certain cases. I
find no mention of this in the rules anywhere. Anyone care to comment?

>9. If the combat is continued by a press is the range determined over
>again or can a minion with a .44 blow away a prince if the prince can not
>get a manuver off?

While it's not explicit in the rulebook section on press, the example
suggests that a new round begins with a default of close range, but
maneuvers can again be used to determine range.

The example says: "He uses the press to extend combat another round.
Cassandra and Tiberius now exchange blows at close range, since
Cassandra has already used the manuver on her handgun." This suggests
to me that (a) there is a maneuver phase, but Cassandra doesn't have
one available, and (b) the default range of the new combat round is
close.

>10. Speaking of princes during a vote do you automaticly get their votes or
>do they have to be untapped? If so does voting tap them?

In the rules section 17.1 voting, you get votes for each *ready* X.

: Good point.  I believe the intent is to alternate 'one-ups' as opposed

Note that only *one* action card may be played, but no limit is set on the
number of action modifier cards that can be played.  No limit on reaction
cards is set, either.

: >2. When a minion plays a political card, just *when* can another minion attempt
: >to block? The rules say before the "terms" of the vote. Does this mean before
: >the political card is actually revealed or before the voting is done?

: After a card is revealed and before the voting is done.

I'm inclined to disagree -- note that the rules state "...must be blocked
before the terms of the vote are set; otherwise, the voting begins."  That
implies to me that the blocking must be done *at least* before a vote is
cast.  Since the play of the card provides a vote, it can be argued that
the voting call must be blocked before revealing the card.

A lot of the political cards have text on them like "divide up four
points between two Methuselahs".  I would say stuff like that is
"setting the terms of the vote".  So, you'd block after the card was
played, but before any of the decisions about *how* it's played are
made.

> 3. Can you play poltical cards during a blood hunt vote to increase
> your votes?

>4. Do you refill your hand immediately after *every* card is played (except
>during voting)? So, during combat you can play a maneuver, then draw, etc...

Some cards explicitly say "don't replace until after this combat".  So
yes, normally, during combat you can play a card that doesn't have
such a restriction on it, draw another one, play it, draw another, et
cetera.

But, IMHO, if such a high percentage of your cards are combat cards
that you can actually get away with this, you're begging to lose.

>5. The rules say that the games take ~3 hours (whatever that means) but it
>would seem to me that the games go quicker since your hand is constantly
>being refilled. What makes the games take longer than Magic?

You can't play cards that fast.  I played my first game last night.
You can play *one* Master card per turn, and each Minion can take one
action per turn.  I never had more than three Minions in play -- it's
*expensive* to bring Minions under your influence, and if you spread
yourself too thin, you become vulnerable.  I went through a lot of
turns without playing any cards at all, just using the cards that were
already down on the table.

In article <3305cb$1kq@rosie.next.com>, Matt Rollefson <rollie@next.com> wrote:
>>8. If the active minion does not play a combat card and then the blocking
>>player does can the active player play one before damage dealing?
>
>This is my big issue currently with the rules: in what order are
>strikes declared? It can make a big difference in certain cases. I
>find no mention of this in the rules anywhere. Anyone care to comment?

Page 31, "Chose Strike":
"If weapons were not used to maneuver, then, after the range is
 determined, the player with the actingin minion first deicdes the
 manner in which the minion is blocking.  Then the blcoking minion can
 respond by either using a weapon or using a strike card."

The example on page 32 clarifies this a little.  If a weapon *was*
used to maneuver, you're forced to use that weapon.  Otherwise, the
vampire who was blocked declares their strike first.  Then the vampire
who's blocking declares their strike.

This is useful to remember: if you use a gun to maneuver, you can't
strike with a thrown sewer lid -- you have to use the gun.

This came up in a game last night, before I'd figured that out.  My
foe blocked one of my Minions, and immediately played a Dodge strike.
But I was going to cast a Tremere ritual on her, and was wondering if
I still needed to burn the card since I knew she was dodging.  So, we
paused playing and looked it up, and since I was active, we decided I
had to declare my strike first.  My ritual went to the ash heap.

sacrifices one of your next Master Phases so you can't play two of them

>The way I read it is this: each Minion decides what they're going to
>do in turn, starting with the Active one.  So, the Active Minion can
>say "I'm going to do a strike with my hands, which requires no card".
>Then the reacting Minion can play a combat card.

Note that this is true for strikes. However, there are various combat
cards which are neither strikes, nor maneuvers, nor presses. For
example, Blur, a card which gives you extra strikes. I would say that
this card can probably be played at any time during the choose strikes
phase and before the resolve damage phase of combat. So it's worth
your while to delay playing it until after the first set of strikes
has been declared, so your opponent doesn't know what's coming.

>>11. Can you use 2 out of turn cards between one turn and the next? What if
>>you would be able to use 2 master cards in a turn?

>This is tricky and came up in a game I played last night.  I decided
>that even out-of-turn Master cards were included in the one Master
>card per turn limit.

>So, for example, I played my "Tremere Chantry" Master card during my
>Master phase, and drew a "Frenzy" out-of-turn Master card to replace
>it.  I wanted to use it during my Minion phase that same turn, but
>decided since I'd already played my Chantry, I couldn't.  If I had a
>card permitting me a second Master action each turn, I'd have decided
>I could have played it.

>I really don't know if this is the right way to do it, but it worked
>last night.

I don't think that this is the right way to do it. The rules (section
7.2.1, Out-of-turn) read: "Out-of-turn cards you play when it is not
your turn; however, if you play an out-of-turn card, you must
sacrifice your master phase for the next round of play. You may not
use another out-of-turn card if you're already used one for your
master phase for the next turn."

I interpret this to mean:

1: You can only play out-of-turn cards when it is not your turn.
2: Using an out-of-turn card sacrifices your entire master phase for
the next turn. Thus even if you had a card that allowed you to play
two master cards per master phase, you would have no master phase and
thus could play no master cards.
3: Once you've sacrificed next turn's master phase, you can't
sacrifice it again, nor can you sacrifice the master phase for the
turn after next.

Rollie

>IMO this should be reversed, and the blocking player should be forced
>to declare their strike first. However, that's the way the rules
>currently read.

It's probably vaguely based on the way combat works in "Vampire: The
Masquerade".

In Vampire, you roll initiative.  The person who loses initiative
*declares* their action first, so the quicker people can "anticipate"
the behavior of the slower ones (then the quicker people actually *do*
their actions first).

In Jyhad, the "active" Minion isn't usually voluntarily entering
combat -- they're trying to do something else, and they're suprised by
the blocking Minion.  So, it would be like the blocking Minion won
initiative, so, the active Minion should declare action first.

I have had this made clear to me in person by the Duelists Convocation
during two tournaments I played in recently.  Playing a Political Card
as a vote is using it as a REACTION card, and hence is illegal.

+ You cannot even play political cards during a call for bloodhunt,

+I have had this made clear to me in person by the Duelists Convocation
+during two tournaments I played in recently.  Playing a Political Card
+as a vote is using it as a REACTION card, and hence is illegal.

  Playing a political card is _not_ a reaction.

  Section 13.2 of the corrected rules: "Reaction cards are played by an
untapped minion and may only be used in response to another player's
minion's actions." Section 17.1 (voting) "When...a call is made for a
bloodhunt... . Additional political cards can also be used by any of the
other Methuselahs for votes" [note: the word 'other' was ruled as not
disqualifiing the one taking the action.]

  Playing a political card for a vote is merely an option you have
duriing a vote which isn't any particular "kind" of action.

  I agree completely that if your judge said it, then that's the way it
should be played for that game. It's still wrong, though. I've frequently
pointed out mistakes judges have made after a match is over. No big deal.

+NO cards may be played for votes during an ordinary call for Bloodhunt
+whatsoever.  None.  All political cards are either actions, reactions,
+or action modifiers.

  I can't find this in my copy of the corrected rules. I can find:

  Section 16.3 (Diablerie), last sentence: "This vote is not considered
an action, so reaction and action modifier cards may not be played."
  Most people read this as a helpful reminder. You can't play 'Bewitching
Oration' on the acting vampire to gain 4 votes since there is no acting
vampire. You can't react with a 'Dread Gaze' to gain 4 votes since (as
quoted above) you can only react to things _minions_ do. If you read it
as a new rule, it still doesn't disqualify action cards, which is what
all the "+1 vote" political cards seem to be.

  To sum up, the rules seem to make a point of saying you can use
political cards for a vote during a bloodhunt in the section on voting,
and don't say you can't in the section on bloodhunts.

Messages.Author: Joshua Bluestein
Messages.Body:
In article <1994Sep9.194928.13055@wdl.loral.com> mab@dst17.wdl.loral.com (Mark A Biggar) writes:

>>In section 17.1 VOTING it says: "When a Political card is played or a
>>call made for a BLOODHUNT against a vampire committing diablerie, a
>>vote is called." This section then goes on the describe the procedure
>>for counting votes, including the use of political actions cards for
>>extra votes.
>>
>>No where in the section does it distinguish a vote for a political
>>action from that for a bloodhunt.  I'd say that the rule are unclear
>>about this.

The bloodhunt is distinguished elsewhere:

Section 16.3 Encounter a Vampire in Torpor (no card required)
Heading Diablerie (no card required)
Paragraph 3:
"...any Methuselah may immediately call a vote among all the
Methuselahs to decide whether or not a bloodhunt will be called.
[...] This vote is not considered an action, so reaction and action
modifier cards cannot be played."

This is a pretty clear nix on Action Mods and Reaction cards.  Action
Mods it makes sense to disallow, since the vote is clearly being
called by the Methuselah and not a Minion.

Reaction cards are probably disallowed for reasons of game balance,
since they can't be played in your own turn (and therefore the
diablerizing Vampire would be at an even greater disadvantage than
before, since most instances of diablerie take plae in the minion's
controller's turn).

The question of Title Votes (Primogen, Prince and Justicar) is more
up for debate.  It's reasonable to believe that they are allowed
since there's no required action on the parts of the minions
themselves, they merely need to be ready.

And, of course, Political Cards, when burned for votes, are not
burned by a minion, they're burned by the Methuselah.

What I'm trying to say is that there is about as much justification
to prevent the use of Political Cards during a bloodhunt vote as
there is to prevent Titled minions from casting votes.  This would
leave a pretty paltry set of options on exactly how one does cast
votes (a set of no options, to be exact).

As such, it seems entirely reasonable (and, indeed, even intuitive)
that Political Cards should be able to be used during bloodhunt
votes.

My $.02
